findings.issue: `pkill -f 'api/server.mjs'` matched the agent's own bash command line and killed its shell (exit 143) — repeated a second time after the cause had already been identified
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID (via `ps`/`ss` output) or bracket the pattern: `pkill -f '[a]pi/server\.mjs'`

findings.issue: Four separate writes shipped with defects (garbage dummy code, missing `const`, invalid template expressions, `<Not found />` markup), each costing an immediate fix turn
findings.suggestion: Compose complete files in one pass and use the edit tool rather than bash+python string replacement for subsequent changes

findings.issue: global.css was written early but never imported into the Layout; all 54 acceptance tests passed on an unstyled app and it was only caught by manual screenshotting
findings.suggestion: Smoke-check rendered output (or a minimal style assertion) before trusting a green test suite

findings.issue: h1 margin-bottom was changed globally (24→16px) to fix the home page, which broke section spacing on other pages, forcing the `.compact-heading` class split
findings.suggestion: Measure the reference once per page type before changing shared rules

findings.issue: After removing `position: sticky`, the agent believed the change hadn't applied and spent several turns re-checking CSS; the browser was serving a stale cached stylesheet
findings.suggestion: Check the loaded stylesheet href/hash (which it eventually did) before suspecting the build

findings.issue: Restarted the app for a visual check without the API running, got fetch-failure errors, briefly guessed 'stale process' before starting the API
findings.suggestion: Keep a startup script that brings up API + app together to avoid environment self-sabotage

findings.issue: Scattered failed bash/read calls: garbage heredoc, `cd /home/pi` fumble, missing PIL, sharp extract out of bounds, nonexistent screenshot path read
findings.suggestion: These were all one-turn recoveries but add up; verify tool availability (which convert/ffmpeg) before scripting against it

summary: A disciplined session: deep up-front recon, a model root-cause debug of the IPv6/localhost binding failure, and visual verification rigorous enough to catch bugs the acceptance tests missed (unstyled app, invisible type pills, wrong sticky header). The main costs were self-inflicted: two self-killing pkill calls, four writes that needed immediate repair, and a long stretch of 1-2px pixel chasing near the end. Final state was fully re-verified — 54/54 tests passing after the last edit.
